_comment: Bean d5f1. One agent's INSPECTION of every extracted image, as data rather than code, so the judgement can be reviewed line by line and re-run. `saw` is the REASON for the role, not the description; `draft` is the description. Every entry here was produced by looking at the image. Applied by scripts/apply-image-verdicts.ts, which writes an `inspection` basis naming this agent and leaves every narrative in `draft` — only a human may confirm one (schemas/narrative.ts). SPLIT 2026-09-20 (bean frs5): this file judged documents that now live in TWO libraries, so it became two files, each beside the documents it judges. A single verdict file spanning libraries is how one library's judgement comes to rewrite another's `images.json` -- `apply-image-verdicts` resolves each document against the library its verdict file is IN, and could not do that from one shared file. Nothing was re-judged: every verdict below is byte-identical to the one it was split from, and `inspected_by`/`inspected_at` are carried over unchanged because the inspection they record actually happened, once, before the split. ADDED 2026-09-29: verdicts for arxiv-2601.22554v1, arxiv-2406.01940v2 and arxiv-2602.16554v1, each produced by opening the image. The file-level `inspected_at` still names the milnorlink inspection because the schema carries one date per file; the three arXiv documents were inspected on 2026-09-29, and this sentence is where that is recorded rather than restamping milnorlink's date.

img-p008-1.saw: Figure 2(a), the blueprint dependency graph of the multivariate Taylor case study, the initial blueprint drafted by the language model
img-p008-1.draft: Figure 2(a): the first blueprint produced for multivariate Taylor's theorem in integral form, before any automated proving. Rectangles are definitions and ellipses are theorems; dashed arrows mark a statement-level use and solid arrows a proof-level use. Definition nodes taylorKernel, taylorRemainderKernel, taylorPoly, lineMap and lineCurve sit at the top; the target frechet_taylor_integral is the sink at the bottom. Most theorem nodes are light blue (unproved); only taylor_integral_one_shot, integrationByParts_smul and ftoc_bochner_wrapper are dark green.

img-p008-2.saw: Figure 2(b), the same graph after the automated prover's first pass
img-p008-2.draft: Figure 2(b): the same initial blueprint after the automated prover's sorry-filling pass. Rectangles are definitions and ellipses are theorems; dashed arrows mark a statement-level use and solid arrows a proof-level use. Definition nodes taylorKernel, taylorRemainderKernel, taylorPoly, lineMap and lineCurve sit at the top; the target frechet_taylor_integral is the sink at the bottom. The leaf lemmas taylorKernel_deriv_t, taylorKernel_at_right and taylorRemainder_eq_explicit have turned dark green; taylor_integral_kernel and lineCurve_iteratedDeriv remain light blue, and taylor_integral_explicit and frechet_taylor_integral are filled a lighter green; the caption distinguishes only blue (unproved) from green (proved), so what the two shades of green separate is not stated in the paper.

img-p008-3.saw: Figure 2(c), the refined blueprint with extra intermediate lemmas, all unproved
img-p008-3.draft: Figure 2(c): the refined blueprint after the planner model decomposed the stuck nodes further. Rectangles are definitions and ellipses are theorems; dashed arrows mark a statement-level use and solid arrows a proof-level use. Definition nodes taylorKernel, taylorRemainderKernel, taylorPoly, lineMap and lineCurve sit at the top; the target frechet_taylor_integral is the sink at the bottom. New intermediate nodes appear -- taylor_remainder_by_parts, taylor_integral_kernel_base, taylorPoly_succ, ftoc_bochner_on_uIcc and lineCurve_contDiffOn_onSeg -- and every theorem node is light blue, i.e. nothing is yet proved in this version.

img-p008-4.saw: Figure 2(d), the refined graph after the second prover pass with three nodes left
img-p008-4.draft: Figure 2(d): the refined blueprint after the prover's second pass. Rectangles are definitions and ellipses are theorems; dashed arrows mark a statement-level use and solid arrows a proof-level use. Definition nodes taylorKernel, taylorRemainderKernel, taylorPoly, lineMap and lineCurve sit at the top; the target frechet_taylor_integral is the sink at the bottom. Nearly every lemma is dark green; three remain light blue -- taylor_remainder_by_parts, lineCurve_iteratedDeriv and frechet_taylor_integral -- which are the nodes the text says were left for a human. taylor_integral_kernel, taylor_integral_explicit and taylor_integral_one_shot are a lighter green.

img-p008-5.saw: Figure 2(e), the completed graph with every node dark green
img-p008-5.draft: Figure 2(e): the completed formalization after a human proved the remaining nodes. Rectangles are definitions and ellipses are theorems; dashed arrows mark a statement-level use and solid arrows a proof-level use. Definition nodes taylorKernel, taylorRemainderKernel, taylorPoly, lineMap and lineCurve sit at the top; the target frechet_taylor_integral is the sink at the bottom. Every theorem node is dark green, meaning the whole graph, including the target frechet_taylor_integral, is proved without sorry.

img-p012-1.saw: Figure 3(a), the rendered blueprint document of the MyNat example
img-p012-1.draft: Figure 3(a): the web blueprint generated from the appendix's MyNat example. It lists Definition 1 (Natural numbers) and Definition 2 (Natural number addition), each with a check mark; Theorem 3, for any natural number a, 0 + a = a, where + is definition 2, with a check mark and a collapsed proof; Theorem 4, (a + 1) + b = (a + b) + 1, with no check mark and the proof text 'Proof by induction on b'; and Theorem 5, a + b = b + a, with no check mark and a proof reading 'The base case follows from theorem 3. The inductive case follows from theorem 4.', both references rendered as links.

img-p012-2.saw: Figure 3(b), the dependency graph of the MyNat example
img-p012-2.draft: Figure 3(b): the dependency graph of the MyNat example. Green rectangles MyNat and nat-add at the top, with dashed arrows from nat-add to a blue-bordered rectangle MyNat.mul and to the ellipses MyNat.succ_add (light blue) and MyNat.zero_add (dark green); solid arrows run from both of those into MyNat.add_comm (light blue), and a dashed arrow from MyNat.mul to a white ellipse MyNat.mul_comm, whose outgoing edge is cut off at the bottom of the image.
